summary: One generic, type-agnostic store for every encrypted vault record, with server-enforced field consistency, optimistic-concurrency versioning, lazy client-side schema migration, and a byte-exact client-built AAD the server never sees.

read.role: the routing layer that answers an administrator session Not Found before any handler here runs, the gate's step 7 that checks the epoch before any handler runs, and the schema trigger that refuses an administrator a records row
what the page does with the Conflict these handlers answer on a replaced epoch: it closes the vault and never reaches a screen's version-reload

sections: Where it lives: inside the vault
read.role: why the fourth record type adds no plaintext column and no AAD byte

accountIdRule.value: required and non-empty exactly for snapshot, empty for every other type. Stated as the complement, so a type added later is empty until something argues otherwise

columnSetIsFixed.value: the column set does not grow per type. A rate record has no plaintext symbol column and no plaintext date column

recordIdFormat.value: client-generated UUIDv4, unique only within one vault. A PUT with a record_id that is not a well-formed UUIDv4 is a Bad Request

nonce.value: 96 bits, fresh per encryption, and must differ from the row's previous nonce on every write

versionRule.value: starts at 1 and increments by exactly 1 per write. A create must carry version 1 with no row already present, an update must carry stored version + 1, anything else is Conflict with nothing written

aadSeparator.value: a single 0x1f byte (ASCII unit separator) joining each field. Required, not cosmetic

aadEncoding.value: each field as UTF-8 text. An empty account_id is the empty string, not the literal null, and still contributes its separator. schema_version and version are unpadded decimal

aadUnchangedByRateType.value: a new record type changes no byte of the encoding. rate carries the empty account_id that account and profile carry, and record_type already varies by type. The fixture is the same fixture

noAadOnTheWire.value: no request or response carries an aad field. A body carrying one is rejected rather than ignored

fieldConsistencyCheck.value: before storing, the server checks the body's recordType, accountId, schemaVersion and version against the path's record_id and against the stored row's immutable columns. recordType never changes, accountId never changes. A mismatch is a Bad Request. POST /api/import runs every record through this same validator

accountIdOnWire.value: null when absent, everywhere: the PUT body, the GET response, and the export file's records. An empty string is a Bad Request rather than a second spelling of absent. The AAD is where null becomes the empty string, on both sides

schemaVersionFloor.value: 1 is the current shape and there is nothing below it, so no migration chain reaches back past it

migrationModel.value: client-side and lazy. On read, decrypt, run an ordered chain of pure functions in memory, use the result immediately, write nothing back. The record persists in the new shape on its next legitimate save, which bumps schema_version and version together. A schema_version higher than the client knows is skipped and counted, never guessed at

list.value: GET /api/records?type=<t>, one type per request, type required and a known value, returning { recordId, recordType, accountId, schemaVersion, version, nonce, ciphertext }

write.value: PUT /api/records/<record_id>, body carries recordType, accountId, schemaVersion, version, nonce, ciphertext

noSingleRecordGet.value: there is deliberately no by-id GET. A stale-version reload refetches that record's whole type

purgeIsElsewhere.value: DELETE /api/accounts/<account_id>?mode=purge is the one type-aware exception and is owned by manage-accounts.md, not this contract

vaultEpochInHandlers.value: each endpoint compares the vault epoch again inside the transaction that reads or writes its rows, a write after BEGIN IMMEDIATE, and answers Conflict {"refused":"vault-replaced"} on a mismatch, writing nothing. The gate's step 7 has already checked it once, and the handler's own compare is what closes the race with an import. Applies to GET, PUT and DELETE alike

versionConflictCarriesNoRefused.value: the Conflict of a stale or occupied version carries no refused member, so vault-replaced is never mistaken for a lost version check. Two tabs writing one record: the second sees that Conflict and reloads. A page holding the replaced DEK sees vault-replaced and closes the vault instead of reloading

replacedEpochReturnsNothing.value: a request carrying a replaced epoch returns no record and leaves records row for row as it was, whatever its method

notOperatorConfig.value: these three are compiled-contract parameters, not operator config, because the Content Too Large tests assert exact behaviour at a boundary

createAtOccupiedIdOrStaleVersion.condition: version is not 1 on a create, or not stored + 1 on an update. The body has no refused member (spec/features/record-api.md#endpoints, spec/features/record-api.md#acceptance-criteria)

vaultReplaced.condition: a GET, a create PUT, an update PUT or a DELETE whose X-Solvent-Vault is not the vault's. The body is {"refused":"vault-replaced"}, nothing is written and no record is returned (spec/features/record-api.md#acceptance-criteria)

vaultHeaderMissingOrMalformed.condition: answered by the gate's step 7 before any handler here, with no refused member (spec/features/app-shell.md#the-request-gate)

recordTypeChanged.condition: a PUT changing an immutable column (spec/features/record-api.md#endpoints)

malformedRecordId.condition: a record_id that is not a well-formed UUIDv4 (spec/features/record-api.md#edge-cases)

accountIdShapeViolation.condition: snapshot with accountId null, any other type with one set, or an accountId of the empty string on any type (spec/features/record-api.md#edge-cases)

accountIdNamesUnknownAccount.condition: the accountId names no account row for this principal (spec/features/record-api.md#edge-cases)

principalIdInBody.condition: a payload carrying a principalId field, rejected outright rather than ignored (spec/features/record-api.md#rules)

aadFieldInBody.condition: a body carrying an aad field (spec/features/record-api.md#the-aad-encoding)

notFoundOrAnotherPrincipalsRecord.condition: Not Found, never Forbidden, so an attacker cannot map which ids exist (spec/features/record-api.md#rules)

administratorSession.condition: every route here is on the vault surface. Not an empty list (spec/features/record-api.md#what-it-does)

fixtures: a stored byte-exact AAD fixture for a known (account_id, record_type, record_id, schema_version, version) tuple, including the empty account_id case, checked in as bytes rather than recomputed by the test
the same stored fixture exercised with and without rate in the type vocabulary, to prove the fourth type moved no byte
two seeded vault owners each holding records of all four types, for the cross-vault isolation and Not-Found-not-Forbidden assertions
a seeded administrator principal and session, for the Not Found assertion on every route here
a record stored at an older schema_version, to assert that reading it leaves version, nonce and ciphertext byte-identical
a record at a schema_version above the client's known version, to assert it is skipped and counted rather than guessed at
a ciphertext at the per-record cap boundary, a vault at the record-count cap, and a user at the byte quota
a vault whose epoch has been replaced (by an import or by replacing the vault_epochs row directly) and a request carrying the epoch from before, for each of GET, create PUT, update PUT and DELETE
a hold on a PUT or DELETE handler between the gate and its transaction, with an import committing at that point, for the race assertion
records captured before and after each replaced-epoch request, row for row, for the writes-nothing assertion
a stale-version write alongside a replaced-epoch write, for the body comparison: one with no refused member and one with vault-replaced
focus: the AAD assertion must run byte for byte against the stored fixture, including every separator and the empty account_id. A test that recomputes the AAD with the same helper it is testing asserts nothing, and the spec asks specifically for the rate-in-vocabulary comparison to be made against the stored fixture rather than against a recomputation

a rejected write of any kind, Conflict, Bad Request or Content Too Large, must leave the stored row byte-identical. Checking only the response code is the easy fake, and the row has to be read back and compared
a principalId or an aad field in a body must be rejected outright, not silently stripped and then ignored. A handler that drops unknown keys passes a behaviour test and fails this rule

accountId must be null and never the empty string in a GET response and in an exported file, asserted against both, because the two are written by different code paths and a shared serializer is an assumption rather than a fact
no log line contains a ciphertext value. This needs the captured log output of a real write, not a grep of the source

an administrator session must get Not Found and not an empty list from GET /api/records. An empty list is the plausible wrong answer and it passes any test that only checks for the absence of another vault's rows

the replaced-epoch assertions must cover GET as well as the writes, each answering vault-replaced with no record in the body and records unchanged row for row. A test of the writes alone passes a read that still hands the old page a vault it cannot decrypt

the race must be asserted by holding the handler after the gate and before its transaction, committing an import at that point, and releasing it: the request answers vault-replaced and writes nothing. The gate's check alone passes every test that does not interleave, and the handler's own compare is the one that closes the race

the Conflict of a stale version must be shown to carry no refused member, and vault-replaced to carry it, by parsing both bodies. A handler that tags every Conflict makes a screen's version reload run on a replaced vault

lazy migration must be shown to write nothing: read a record at an older schema_version and compare version, nonce and ciphertext before and after, rather than only checking that the decrypted payload came out in the new shape
